INTRODUCING CLARA

Good products deserve a clearer story.

Why we’re building an AI marketing team that starts with what your team already knows.

Clara · Abstract Machines

PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE → POSSIBILITYSomething good.
Worth sharing.

The story is already there

A product team rarely starts with nothing to say. There are design decisions in a document, useful explanations in a support reply, and small improvements in a release note. The hard part is gathering those details and shaping them into something another person can understand.

That work often arrives at the end of an already full week. A launch needs an article. An improvement deserves a post. A recurring customer question could become a tutorial. Each one asks someone to rebuild the context before they can write.

Start with the product

Clara begins with that context: your product sources, your audience, and your voice. The goal is to give your team a place to turn what it knows into work it can review and share.

We’re starting with content. Articles, social posts, release notes, and connected campaigns give an idea different ways to reach people. Carousels and video make room for stories that need to be seen as well as read.

A teammate needs direction

A brief still matters. So does deciding which story is worth telling. Clara can help develop a draft, but your team knows the customer, the tradeoffs, and the details that make a claim accurate.

That is why you choose where review belongs in the workflow. Assistant offers suggestions, Co-pilot handles internal work and asks before publishing, and Autopilot can carry permitted work through automatically. Your team sets the boundaries and keeps approval where it matters.

What we’re building toward

Clara is a product from Abstract Machines, the team behind Atomic. Atomic helps turn ideas into applications. Clara addresses the next challenge: helping people understand the things you’ve built.

Clara now brings that context to a team of agents, with repeatable workflows for content, social activity, search visibility, and competitor research. Schedules, events, and configurable autonomy let the work continue beyond a single brief. We’re preparing early access and learning where that combination is most useful.
